The IMF Programs Dataset records participation in IMF lending programs in {{< dataset-value period >}}. The raw dataset lists {{< dataset-value counts.arrangements >}} arrangements and outright purchases for {{< dataset-value counts.members >}} IMF members, with their facilities, dates, and amounts. Most come from the IMF's History of Lending Commitments page; the other {{< dataset-value counts.added >}} come from IMF press releases, Executive Board documents, and other IMF publications. The panel dataset turns {{< dataset-value counts.panel_arrangements >}} of these arrangements into yearly indicators for {{< dataset-value counts.states >}} independent states: months under a program, and whether one was in force, for all, concessional, and non-concessional programs. The codebook explains how the data were collected and built.

## Figures

<!-- Drawn by R/fig-programs-participation.R from the panel dataset. After a
     new release, rerun it and check the alt text against the numbers it
     prints. Phones get the -narrow image. -->

::: {#fig-programs-participation}
```{=html}
<picture>
<source media="(max-width: 575.98px)" srcset="../images/figures/programs-participation-narrow.png" width="720" height="600">
<img src="../images/figures/programs-participation.png" width="1600" height="720" class="img-fluid" alt="Line chart of the number of states with an IMF program in force each year from 1952 to 2025, for all programs, concessional programs, and non-concessional programs. The total rises from 2 in 1952 to a peak of 75 in 1996, falls to 41 in 2007 and 40 in 2018, and stands at 55 in 2025. Concessional programs begin in 1986 and outnumber non-concessional ones in every year from 1997 to 2015.">
</picture>
```

States with an IMF program in force at any time in the year, {{< dataset-value period >}}, from the panel dataset. A state can have a concessional and a non-concessional program in the same year, so those two lines can add up to more than all programs. No concessional program was in force before 1986, so until then the lines for all programs and non-concessional programs coincide. Rapid disbursements and outright purchases are left out.
:::
